x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: Krishnadevaraya renovated Srikalahasti, and its gali gopuram collapsed in 2010. Statement 3 is wrong: Ahobilam's Narasimha Swamy temple was developed in the late Vijayanagara phase, not the early Chola period. Hence 1 and 2 only.

The Lotus Mahal is lotus-shaped with domes in Indo-Islamic (Indo-Arabic) style. The Huzur Daftar was the 40-pillared council chamber (not a stepped tank), the Queen's Bath stood near the Lotus Mahal in the zenana area (it was not a council chamber), and the Mahanavami Dibba was the platform for the Dasara festival (not elephant stables).

The Chintala Venkataramana and Bugga Ramalingeswara temples are at Tadipatri. The Upper and Lower Narasimha temples are at Ahobilam (not Kadiri), Mallikarjuna is the deity of Srisailam (not Tirupati), and Venkateswara is the deity of Tirupati (not Ahobilam).

Srisailam, Tripurantakam and Srikalahasti were the Shaiva centres. Kanchi, Mangalagiri and Pushpagiri were Vaishnava centres; Tirupati, Ahobilam and Kadiri were Vaishnava/Narasimha centres; and D mixes Penugonda (Vasavi Kanyaka Parameswari), Amaravati (Smarta Shaiva) and Tirumala (Vaishnava).

Asadi Katha uses the Javiki and Chedika. Jeganta (large bells) and ankle bells belong to the Bhagavatulu, not Harikatha (which uses Chidatalu); the oggu drum belongs to Oggu Katha; and Pichukuntla Katha performers use turban, sword and shield while singing Palnati Veeracharitra.
All four pairs are correct: Hanuman appears on the coins of Harihara and Bukka, Venkateswara and Balakrishna on Krishnadevaraya's, Garuda on Achyutaraya's and Varaha on Tirumala Raya's.
All four statements are correct: legends were in Devanagari; the varaha (pagoda) was the largest gold coin; Tar and Pesado were silver; Jital and Kasu were copper.

Sankranti falls in January and features Gangireddulaata, Kolla Pandalu (cockfights) and Pottella Pandalu (ram fights). Atla Taddi is a women's festival of Ashwayuja, Ugadi is the Telugu New Year (19 March in 2026), and Vasantotsavam was the most popular festival under the Reddi kings.
